section "Closing check C1" (N-c1c-1, N-c1c-2) of `checks/M0-a-11-notes.md`.

* **Before-image.** No seat runs git, and the builder's before-mirror was removed. The pre-round sources are main's
  committed files: this seat fetched the item's 19 owned files and `num/exact.ts`, `num/index.ts`, `src/index.ts` at
  main's head `6e1655b` (the last commit touching `src/skeleton/` is `b8e0341`, the S1 + S2 round) with
  `gh api -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw" repos/…/contents/plat/<path>?ref=6e1655b…` (read-only, the GitHub
  contents API). 10 owned files equal the tree. The nine that differ are exactly the round's: `src/skeleton/{prepare,
  roof,engine,types,index}.ts` and `test/skeleton/{contract,downgrade,spur,translation}.test.ts`; `golden.test.ts` is

  mutant; for the before-runs the five pre-round sources were swapped in, then the round's restored (`diff -r` of the
  mirror's `src/skeleton` against the tree: no difference). Its `node_modules` were deleted at the end.

winds twice (a pentagram) …'. **H1 / H3 equivalence**: CONFIRMED by execution — `zzc-wraps.test.ts` over 12 232 rings
that turn left everywhere (every {n/k} star polygon for n ≤ 13 at three radii and four phases, every start and both
orientations, plus 4 000 rectangles with a collinear mid-edge vertex, axis-aligned and rotated): the digest of every
`convexNearRectangle` result is `98e46704…` on the round's code, under H1 and under H3; the probe is sensitive (W0
moves it to `b51082a9…`, 480 more passes). The argument (PLAUSIBLE, reasoned): with every turn in [0, π) the
direction rotates monotonically counter-clockwise, so the number of 1 → 0 steps across any half-open split of the
circle by a line through the origin is the turning number. The engine's use is not so free (H4 – H7 red).

## Comments, read against the code

* `prepare.ts:1–10` (module): the pre-clean order (repeats; then spurs and collinear merge to a fixpoint) is
  `prepareRings`'s loop `mergeCollinear(dropSpurs(cleaned))` until the length is unchanged; orientation, canonical
  start and the six refusals are the code's; "the contact and containment tests are the kernel's shared exact
  predicates (`num/exact.ts`, C-0314)" — `segmentsMeet` and `insideRing` now call exactly those. C-0276 and C-0283
  exist and say this.
* `prepare.ts:52–61` (`dropSpurs`): "the tip and the second of its two coincident neighbours in walk order are removed,
  the first kept" is the main loop (`out` ends a, b and s = a: pop b, skip s, keep a); "read cyclically from the tip: a
  tip at the walk's last vertex keeps the root's visit just before it" is the seam's first case (`same(out[n−2],
  out[0])`: pop the tip `out[n−1]`, shift `out[0]`, keep `out[n−2]`), and the second case keeps `out[n−1]`, the visit
  before the tip `out[0]` — C-0283 (2)'s `[R, P1, P2, P3, R, T]` example and M14's pin agree.
* `prepare.ts:125–131` (`segmentsMeet`): "a proper crossing, or an end of one on the other (a touch at an end and a
  collinear overlap count)" — exact.ts's body; a collinear overlap always puts an end of one segment on the other.
* `prepare.ts:157–165` (`insideRing`): "defined for a point on none of the ring's edges: `prepareRings` asks only a
  hole's first vertex, after `ringsMeet` has refused every contact" — the code checks `holeContact` (line 218)
  before `holeOutside` (lines 222–223) and passes `pts[k][0]`.
* `types.ts:29–34` (`SkeletonEdge`'s doc): "a spur's root keeps its first visit in walk order, read cyclically from the tip,
  C-0283 (2)" — the same rule in C-0283's words; `from`/`to` are built from the kept `Src.i` (`prepare.ts:233`).
* `skeleton/index.ts:1–2`: the description and the item id; the scaffold sentence gone.
* The four test headers and the two inline comments say what the cases assert (C-0276 (1), C-0276 (4), C-0171); every
  describe / it title is unchanged (the titles still carry "(session fix S2, M13)" / "(S2, M14)", as titles must).
* `golden.test.ts` (new): its six faces are what its header says — corpus faces 556 and 1236 (the file's offsets added:
  identical rings) and `holedPolygons(1)` faces 137, 189, 261, 331 (generated: identical rings, on a 50 cm grid).
